blocks.text: Onboarding an Azure DevOps organization to AI Security Admin Portal connects your organization’s Azure DevOps environment (organizations and projects) to the AI Security Admin Portal. This connection enables AI Security to discover, assess, and help you govern AI-related activity and risks across your codebase.

When onboarding, you must select an authentication type to establish a secure connection between Zscaler and Azure DevOps. You can choose either Client Secret, which uses a shared secret key generated in your Azure app registration, or Certificate, which uses a PEM file for certificate-based authentication. The authentication type you select determines the credentials you need to provide during the onboarding process.
Before onboarding a Azure DevOps organization, ensure you have completed the following:

blocks.item: 1. Registered an app in the Azure Portal.
To create an app in Entra ID:
Sign in to the Azure portal.
Go to App Registrations.
Click + New registration.
See image.
In the Register an application page:
Name: Enter a unique name for the application.
Supported account types: Retain the default selection.
Click Register.
See image.

The application is registered and details are displayed in the Essentials section of the Overview page. Copy the Application (client) ID details, Directory (Tenant ID), and ensure you have saved the details. The client ID is required while updating the Configuration Details in the AI Security Admin Portal.
See image.
2. Granted access to your organization.
To grant an organization access, do the following:
In Azure DevOps, go to Organization Settings > Users.
Select Organization Settings > Users > Add new users.
See image.
Click Add new users.
In the Add new users drawer, enter the following:
Users or Service Principals: Select the User or Service Principal created via the app registration.
Access level: Select the access level as Basic.
Add to Projects: Select the projects you want to add.
Azure DevOps Groups: Assign the user to the required projects with Project Reader permissions (minimum required).
Click Add.
See image.
The user is added to the organization. Use this while onboarding your Azure DevOps organization.

blocks.text: To onboard an Azure DevOps organization, do the following:

blocks.item: Go to Administration > Account Onboarding.
Click + Add New.
The Start Onboarding window appears.
Select Code Repository.
See image.
In the Select Code Repository window, select the Azure DevOps tile.
See image.
The Add Azure DevOps Organization page appears.
In the Configuration window, do the following:
Tenant Alias: Enter a unique name for the tenant as registered in the Azure DevOps Portal.
Tenant ID: Enter the Microsoft Entra tenant ID.
Organization Name: Enter the name of the organization that you created in the Azure DevOps Portal.
Authentication Type: Select one of the following from the drop-down menu.
Client Secret
Enter the following information:
Client ID: The Application (client) ID you copied and saved from the Overview page in the Azure portal.
Client Secret: The client secret created for the app registration. To create a client secret, do the following:
In the Microsoft Entra admin center or Azure portal, click the newly created application.
In the left-side navigation, go to Manage > Certificates & secrets.
In the Client secrets tab, click + New client secret.
In the Add a client secret drawer:
Description: Enter a description for the client secret.
Expires: Select the expiration time from the drop-down menu. By default, 180 days (6 months) is selected.
Click Add.
See image.
The client secret is generated and displayed.
See image.
Copy the secret immediately and paste it in the Client Secret field in the Configuration window in AI Security.
Click Save.
See image.
Client Certificate
Enter the following information:
Client ID: The Application (client) ID you copied and saved from the Overview page in the Azure portal.
See image.
Click Save & Next.
The system generates a PEM file.
Click Download Certificate to download the certificate as a PEM file.
In the Azure portal, go to App registration > Certificates & secrets > Certificates and upload the certificate.
See image.
Click Validate to confirm that Zscaler can successfully authenticate with the connection.
See image.
Return to the Account Onboarding page to verify onboarding.

blocks.text: After successful onboarding, access to any projects created subsequently is not granted automatically. The user or service principal must be manually granted access to each new project. You can also run an On-Demand Validation if you require your projects to be discovered immediately.
To grant access to a newly created project, do the following:

blocks.item: Go to Azure DevOps > Organization Settings > Users.
Select the user or service principal created during onboarding.
Click Manage Access Level.
Under Projects, select the newly created project. You can select more than one project at a time.
Click Save.

blocks.text: To discover newly added projects immediately in Zscaler, do the following:

blocks.item: In the AI Security portal, go to Administration > Account Onboarding.
Select the Azure DevOps integration.
Click Manage.
Select On-Demand Validation to initiate immediate discovery of newly added projects. To learn more, see Managing Code Repository Integrations.

blocks.text: If immediate discovery is not required, Zscaler automatically checks for new repositories twice a day, at 12:00 AM and 12:00 PM UTC.
